_comment: Hand corrections to the reader's output for A6, in pixels of the
full-resolution crops in .build/a6/ (see imageSize / sheetImageSize).
THE BOARD. The reader found 354 of the 423 designators, 84% -- or 88% of
the 405 that have a silkscreen designator at all, since E6 and the H and MP
parts are a plug-in shorting header, spacers, a screw, rivets, clamps,
ejectors, a label, two shields and a cable, none of them lettered anywhere.
Every one of the 354 was rendered and looked at, and 41 were wrong:
agreed    237 of 243 right   (C21 on C212, C44 on C49, L4 on L9, L6 on
C506, Q4 on Q9, Q9 on C509)
ambiguous  28 of 39 right
single     25 of 29 right
collision  23 of 43 right
which is the usual shape: agreed is the best tier and still not a clean
one. The collision tier is the interesting one here, because on this board
it has a single cause and a single answer: every one of its twenty errors
is a designator read off a LONGER designator's label -- C20 off C209, C30
off C306, C40 off C406, R21 off R212, R74 off R79, R404 off R401, U14 off
U11 -- and in every pair the longer one was right. This board is full of
three-digit filter designators (C1xx-C5xx, Q1xx-Q5xx, R1xx-R5xx) sitting
beside their two-digit counterparts, which is exactly the artwork that
produces a truncation misread.
Fourteen of the wrong markers name parts §5-5, its onFail lists or the
caveats point at, so those are replaced by hand below; the rest are
dropped, and the coverage badge then tells the truth about them.
All twelve test points are placed by hand as a matter of course. Each is
drawn as a short bar with its label beside, above or below it, and the
offset is not constant: TP1's bar is 48 px right of its label, TP15's is
150 px below, TP16's is 54 px above and TP11's is 127 px below. Each box
spans bar and label together -- a marker on the label alone sends a probe
to the wrong place, which is the one error this tool must not make.
THE SHEETS. Sheet 1 is the supplies, the 8 MHz clock and the phase-locked
loop; sheet 2 the amplitude control amplifier, the X10 stage and the
output; sheet 3 the five octave filters and their switch drive. Every
marker on all three was reviewed:
sh1  144 read   107 kept   37 rejected   +  6 placed by hand   = 113
sh2   68 read    50 kept   18 rejected   +  2 placed by hand   =  52
sh3  168 read   124 kept   44 rejected                          = 124
and the rejects are the shapes the pipeline has met before. Sheet 1 has
two blocks that are pure designators laid out in a grid and both read as
confident placements: the transistor package legends ('Q8,Q9, Q101,Q105,
Q201,Q205, ...' beside a TOP view, which produced Q2, Q301, Q305, Q502 and
C407) and the CD4028 decoder U8, whose output pins are literally labelled
Q0 to Q9 (which produced Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7, Q8 and Q9 -- seven markers,
all in the agreed or ambiguous tier). Find those two blocks before
reviewing anything else on this sheet. The rest are the usual: pin numbers
read as designators (L11 off U1 pin 11, L15 off '15', C110 off '9'/'5',
H5 off U14D's 8/9), net names and captions (H1 off 'PLL DIAGNOSTICS', MP8
off '(PG2C8)', Z1 off the word CARBON, L1 off the '=' in the test point
legend), and part values (MP1 off 'MF', L2 off 'Z2', R36 off 'BFR96',
VR1 off '5.6uH').
Sheet 3 loses most of its non-agreed reads to a third pattern the other
sheets do not have: this sheet draws five near-identical filter sections,
so a two-digit designator is read off a three-digit one on almost every
one of them -- C1 off Z1's pins, C2 off '100', C3 off C203, C5 off C503,
C29 off C509, C53 off C503, R5 off R505, R52 off R502, R53 off R503, R55
off R505, Q3 off Q9, Q5 off R413. Twenty-two of its twenty-six ambiguous
markers and eleven of its 124 agreed ones went that way.
The test points are the reason the sheet work matters. All twelve are
written twice on sheet 1 -- once in the legend box at the top right, once
beside the flag on their own net -- and the reader prefers the legend,
because it is crisper text in a neat column. build_coords caught six of
them; the rest are placed by hand here, on the flag. TP4 and TP16 were the
only two the reader put on the net by itself, and both are kept as read.
TP11, TP12, TP13, TP14 and TP17 live on sheet 2, where the reader placed
all five on their flags correctly, so their sheet 1 legend rows are simply
dropped.
A later pass closed the board's remaining 75 gaps -- the 23 markers dropped
above as truncation misreads plus 52 designators the reader never found.
Every one was measured by eye off a labelled pixel grid over
.build/a6/drawing_full.png and rendered back before it was written; all 75
have a silkscreen designator, so nothing went to notOnDrawing and the board
now stands at 405 of 405 letterable parts. The five repeated filter blocks
(1xx-5xx) locate a part but do not place it: the blocks are similar and NOT
identical -- C108 sits beside R116 where C208 sits on its own, C405's label
is printed to the LEFT of its body because Q402's outline crowds it, and the
3xx block shifts C302 and R302 ~200 px right around C51 -- so each was
measured in its own block. Q204 is drawn as a circle to match Q104/Q304/
Q404/Q504 (a Hough fit seeded from the label ran away onto C211's lettering,
so its 94 px body was measured by eye against the four arcs); U14 is the
flood-filled DIP outline, the same shape as U1-U15. Everything else is a box
on the designator text, which is what the rest of this board's markers are.

The first six are parts that are in notOnDrawing below: listing a part
there does NOT remove a marker the reader already made for it, so a
no-silkscreen part with a bogus placement stays placed and stays wrong.
H6 was the worst of them -- a 500 x 550 px box over the vco, which
check_data reported as containing CR1, CR2, L5 and U3.
The rest are truncation misreads: a two-digit designator read off a
_notOnDrawingComment: Parts with no silkscreen designator anywhere on the artwork. E6 is the
plug-in shorting header that lives on J6 and has no footprint of its own;
H1-H5 are the Rev-9-only TO-5 transistor mounting spacers; H6 is the C-MOS
handling label; H10 a screw; MP1 and MP2 the front and rear shields; MP5,
MP11 and MP12 adhesive cable clamps; MP6 and MP7 rivets; MP8 and MP9 the
two nylon ejectors, which are drawn but never lettered; and MP10 the 75
ohm coaxial cable to A5. They stay searchable in the parts list, but
counting them as unplaced would make the coverage badge lie.
_dropSchematicComment: Sheet reads reviewed by eye and rejected, grouped per sheet. Anything
replaced by a hand placement below is not listed here.
_schematicComment: Hand placements on the sheets, in pixels of the sheet's own crop. Five of
sheet 1's test points had been placed on the legend box rather than on
their net; those five plus U10, whose label the reader missed entirely,
are placed here. On sheet 2 the coax connector J1 and the CA1302
amplitude control amplifier U9 are placed: J1's read was on U9's pin 11
and U9's own read was rejected as a collision, so neither was placed at
all -- and U9 pin 6 is the point §5-5 step 11 measures.
Each placement was checked against the signal name printed beside the
flag: TP1 sits on 8MHz REFERENCE, TP2 on the PLL filter output between J6
and R6, TP3 on U3's pin 3 through R11, TP10 on 1-32MHZ OUTPUT above R70,
TP15 on the F IN net into U1 pin 3. All five agree with the legend.
A later pass placed the 102 parts that had a board position and no
schematic one: 15 on sheet 1, 12 on sheet 2 and 75 on sheet 3. Sheet 3
draws the same filter channel five times over (1xx at the top through
5xx at the bottom) and the five blocks are similar but NOT identical --
the FET and the left-hand divider sit 20-100 px differently in each --
so each label was measured in its own band rather than copied down from
the channel above. Every position was rendered back onto the sheet and
looked at before it was written, and the 46 that tesseract never found
at all were searched for a second time with the vision model. Nothing
here comes from a legend: sheet 1 carries a TP table and a block of
transistor bottom-view pinouts in its top-right corner (both already
emptied by the earlier review) and no marker sits inside either.
A third pass placed the 20 parts that had neither a board nor a sheet
position: seven on sheet 1 (C30, C32, C57, CR9, L4, R9, R70), four on sheet
2 (C40, C42, C61, R49) and nine on sheet 3 (C101, C203, C311, C405, CR103,
CR502, Q204, R214, R501). Each was found from its neighbours' sheets, read
off a pixel grid over the sheet's own crop and rendered back: every one sits
on the designator beside its symbol on the net, none in the TP table or the
transistor pinout block. Which sheet a part is on does not follow its
number -- C30, C32 and C57 are supply decouplers on sheet 1 while C40, C42
and C61 are on sheet 2, and R70 is on sheet 1 under the 1-32MHZ OUTPUT flag
although R68, R69 and R71 are all on sheet 2.

_sheetsComment: Zone grids. The crops were measured to the OUTER rule of each D-sheet
frame, so the inner border -- the one the zone letters and numbers are
divided against -- sits about 60 px inside it on every edge. On sheets 1
and 3 the frame's left border is at or off x=0 in the scan, which is why
their x0 is so much smaller than sheet 2's.
_layersComment: Registering the photograph against the locator drawing. Four landmark
pairs, one per corner, taken from the board's four MOUNTING HOLES rather
than from silkscreen, and the alignment is marked approximate because of
it: four corner pairs constrain the frame and say nothing about the
middle.
The mounting holes were chosen deliberately over the usual answer. The
silkscreen designator text on this board does NOT sit where the drawing
prints it -- J1 is the clearest case, its label printed to the RIGHT of
the connector body on the drawing and to the LEFT of it on the board, a
shift of about 350 drawing px -- so a landmark taken from lettering would
have been a measurement of Fluke's typesetting rather than of the board.
A mounting hole is a hole in the laminate: it is in the board plane, it
has no parallax, and it is the same physical point in both pictures. The
pitfall about mounting holes is about the STANDOFFS that sit in them; on
this photograph all four holes are empty.
Checked afterwards by mapping twenty reviewed board coordinates through
the solved matrix and rendering them on the photograph: U5, U6, U9, U13,
Z1, Z2, J1, L6, Q9, TP11, TP13, TP14, TP16, TP17 and the four 4.7 uF
tantalums all land on their parts. Two independent points measured by
hand -- TP17's and TP14's loop bars -- come out 6 and 7 photo px from
where they were measured. Good enough to line the two views up; not a
cross-correlated fit, which is why it says approximate.
